newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady on Wall St, bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady on Wall St, bonds.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were mixed to slightly higher on Monday, taking strength from Wall Street's eight consecutive record on Friday and higher Treasury prices.
"Bonds are firm and press comment over the weekend on Wall Street seemed more bullish than of late..perhaps people are warming to it," one London dealer said.
The Dow rose 0.55 percent to 6,348.03 points on Friday, its eight consecutive record, driven by heavy gains in IBM.
London dealers said the index was likely to edge slightly higher if Treasuries held their gains but said they were increasingly nervous of a potential correction.
"It's becoming very hard to call...we would like to see the market come off, even a couple of hundred points and then we'd be less nervous about it," one trader said.
Dealers described the London market as quiet.
Among movers, oil group Texaco was up $1/4 at $101-3/8 on news it settled a racial discrimation lawsuit.
IBM, which soared on Friday, was hit by profit-taking in London, trading $3/4 lower at $144-1/4.
Boeing was up $3/4 at $92-1/2 on news the Pentagon had chosen it and Lockheed Martin Corp to make demonstration models of the proposed Joint Strike Fighter.
"This is quite a coup from Boeing and means a shift away from the civil aviation side," the first dealer said.
Hewlett Packard was down $3/8 at $50-1/2 ahead of its quarterly results. Among carmakers, General Motors was up $1/4 at $55-3/4 on talk the company is considering raising dividends, traders said.
